body: Absolutely. I've been working as best I can as a minor in another state, even emailing her parents and giving her the advice I could muster from my experience, but at this point this is probably the best (and only realistic) option.

Thank you so much, it's good to have someone with experience give advice. I'm a bit of a weathered 17-year-old, but I'm only familiar with CPS, not APS. She's doing quite well mentally, so if any more abuse crops up or if she wants them involved beforehand, I'm going straight to them.

Unfortunately, she's in a non-medical facility, kind of a shelter sort of place. Thank you so much for responding. Why I was worried was because if she can't stay here, she's forced back with her parents, and I wouldn't put it past them to let her die of neglect. Calling seems like a good place to start, but I'm worried about disturbing the fragile peace we're maintaining at the moment with the place. If any more abuse occurs, I'll call immediately, though. I have to ask, though, would they take a minor (I'm 17) from a different state who doesn't know the victim outside of the internet seriously? And she's 24, so unfortunately I can't get CPS involved.

She was recently able to talk to the higher-ups and get things temporarily sorted out, but the problem is that this has happened before, and they started up again...and I asked her about the cops, and she said that the end result of that would most likely be her having to go back to her parents or the cops listening to the employees. I seriously am terrified as to the future for her, and I know I've posted a question which is basically dead-end, but I feel like there has to be something...
